216: (26) Oil with fragrance – This means that fragrance was added to the oil so that the oil itself smells. The same applies to water and other liquids that have had fragrance added to them.

(27) Like the anointing oil – The intention is not that it was made in the exact quantity or measure like the anointing oil (shemen hamishchah), because that is forbidden, but rather to show that it is customary to perfume oil with fragrances, as we find with the anointing oil, which was perfumed.
(28) Trees and fragrances – This refers to both fragrant herbs and other kinds of fragrances.

(29) If it was filtered – This means that we are referring to cases where some of the fragrance still remains in the oil. Therefore, a blessing is recited over that specific type of fragrance. However, if it was filtered to the point that the fragrance is entirely removed, no blessing is recited.
(30) “Who creates pleasant oil” – The same as with persimmon oil (shemen afarsimon).

(31) Has no substance – This refers to a weak fragrance that is not substantial enough to warrant a blessing. This is similar to what is explained later in Siman 217, regarding smelling fragrances from tools used for incense.

(32) Avoid smelling it – In order not to put oneself in doubt about a blessing. This applies when there is only this particular fragrance available. However, when other fragrances are available, one should recite a blessing on them, such as “Who creates fragrant trees” or “Who creates various kinds of fragrances”. Some authorities conclude that if one does not want to be strict, it is allowed to smell and recite “Who creates various kinds of fragrances”. Additionally, it should be noted that on Yom Kippur, certain spirituous fragrances are often smelled without reciting a blessing, and it is even forbidden to place these on linen garments, as it causes the fabric to absorb the fragrance. Regarding perfume, known as shlakvasser (yiddish term often used to describe artificial fragrances or synthetic scents, no blessing should be recited over it, as it does not emit a proper fragrance.
